kill.text: Price below $120: thesis on data-centre on-site power under stress; re-review
2027 revenue guide implies growth below 40% or backlog shrinks
New equity or convertible issuance above 5% of shares

sections.industry_map: Bloom makes solid-oxide fuel cells that generate electricity on site from natural gas (or hydrogen), sold to data centres, utilities (AEP), and industrial users, and financed via partners such as Brookfield.
sections.size_growth: On-site power for data centres is a new, fast-growing market because grid connections take 3-7 years. Bloom guides 2026 revenue $4.4-4.6B (+~122%); Q3 2026 revenue $1.24B (+138%), operating margin 18% (company results via renewable-energy-industry.com, 23 Oct 2026). Highly cyclical with AI capex and gas prices.
sections.structure: Competes with gas turbines and reciprocating engines (GE Vernova, Caterpillar, Wärtsilä), batteries plus grid, and future small nuclear. Bloom wins on speed to power (months, not years).
sections.demand_supply: Demand: Oracle framework up to 2.8 GW (1.2 GW firm), Brookfield $25B financing, NTT DATA 900 MW from 2027. Supply: Bloom is expanding factory capacity; constraint is manufacturing ramp and gas supply. Call: shortage of fast power through 2027-28.
sections.industry_risks: (1) Data-centre approvals slow after the Democrat midterm sweep (3 Nov 2026) and a promised Texas moratorium - medium/high; warning: state rules. 97% of Q3 revenue was US. (2) AI capex slowdown - medium/high. (3) Natural gas price spikes - medium/medium. (4) Competition from turbines as their supply catches up - medium/medium by 2028.
sections.outlook: Near: very strong 2026 numbers but post-election selling (-16% on 6 Nov). Mid: consensus EPS rising to ~$8.24 by 2028. Long: depends on whether on-site fuel cells become a standard data-centre power layer or a bridge until grid capacity arrives.
sections.winners: Speed to power, cost per MWh vs grid, financing partners, factory scale, fuel flexibility.
sections.business: Product revenue $1.07B of Q3's $1.24B; adjusted EBITDA $300M; net income $250M; but free cash flow -$181M as working capital builds. Interest cover only 1.4x and dilution ~8.5% a year historically (ValueInvestor research).
sections.right_to_win: Bloom is the only fuel-cell maker with proven multi-hundred-MW deliveries and bankable financing partners, and it can deliver power in months.
sections.moat: Narrow at best: technology and installed base, but turbines and engines compete on price. Trend: improving with scale.
sections.tam_competitors: Small share of total power equipment but leading share of on-site data-centre fuel cells. Competitors: GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Caterpillar, FuelCell Energy.
sections.management: Founder-CEO KR Sridhar (since 2001). History of losses until 2024; now profitable. Insiders net sellers ($46M over 6 months). Funding via convertibles has diluted holders.
sections.financials: Revenue $794M (2020) to $2.0B (2025) and ~$4.5B in 2026; operating margin from -22% (2022) to +18% (Q3 2026). FCF negative most years. Share count rising ~8.5% a year.
sections.company_risks: (1) Customer concentration (Oracle, Brookfield) - KPI: top-customer share. (2) Cash conversion - KPI: FCF. (3) Dilution - KPI: share count. (4) Policy - KPI: US data-centre approvals.
sections.variant_view: The market treats Bloom as an AI-power winner worth ~34x forward earnings; we agree the business has turned, but the price already assumes several years of hyper-growth with negative cash flow and policy risk, so we do not add and would trim into strength.
sections.valuation: Our value (owner earnings $3.2/share, 32% then 12%, 13% discount): low $70, base $130, high $190; price $173 is 33% above base. Street mean $284 (26 analysts), based on 2028 EPS of ~$8.24. Required margin of safety 50% (high-growth, early) gives entry $65. Ming's cost $182.50 (-5%). Verdict PASS means do not add; consider trimming rather than a full sale given the strong operating momentum.
sections.pillars: (1) 2027 revenue growth above 40% - breach below 30%. (2) Operating margin above 15% - breach below 10%. (3) FCF positive in 2027 - breach: negative. (4) Diversification beyond Oracle/US - breach: one customer above 40% of revenue.
sections.catalysts_flow: Q4 2026 results and 2027 guide (Feb 2027); NTT shipments from 2027; state data-centre policy moves. Sellers: momentum funds after the election. Buyers: energy-transition and AI-power funds on dips.
sections.premortem: (1) Data-centre moratoria and AI capex cuts stall orders in 2027. (2) Turbine supply catches up and undercuts Bloom on cost. (3) Cash burn forces another dilutive raise.
